body:
The sentence "This reflects modern common industry practice but is backed by increasing timeouts when multi-factor or stronger authenticators are used." is a bit hard to understand and it's unclear what is meant by "backed by increasing timeouts when multi-factor or stronger authenticators are used."

Do we mean that stronger forms of authentication justifies a longer timeout? If so, why? If anything, I think it should be the opposite, e.g., the longer since the user proved their identity with strong MFA, the less assurance we have that it's the same user behind that session. The high assurance of identity we initially had is not worth much if the user left the computer/device unlocked and the application has been idle for hours.
title: V3.3 - "backed by increasing timeouts when multi-factor or stronger", unclear justification?
